name: VK2735

lead: VK2735 is an investigational dual agonist of the GLP-1 and GIP receptors, aimed at strong fat loss and a leaner look. People seeking large fat loss watch it as a rival to tirzepatide, which acts on the same pair of receptors.

By activating those receptors it reduces appetite and affects metabolism, so body fat falls. In a 13-week phase 2 trial in adults with obesity or overweight, mean weight loss ranged from 9.1% to 14.7% depending on dose, versus 1.7% with placebo. Phase 3 trials began in 2025.

paras: Viking Therapeutics is testing it as a weekly injection and as a daily oral tablet. It is available only through clinical trials, and no use outside medical studies for appearance has been documented.
Safety is still being assessed in phase 3. The 13-week phase 2 trial was short, so long-term effects are unknown, and it is not approved as a medicine.

angle.text: VK2735 is an investigational GLP-1/GIP injection watched by people seeking strong fat loss. It shrinks appetite, lowering body fat and giving a leaner look. A 13-week phase 2 trial reported roughly 9 to 15 percent weight loss, and phase 3 is underway.

lead: VK2735 is an investigational dual agonist of the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptors, developed by Viking Therapeutics for weight management. It is being tested as a weekly subcutaneous injection and as a daily oral formulation, and is not approved as a medicine.[1][2][3][4][5] For appearance, the interest is body composition: drugs of this type lower appetite and body weight, and loss of body fat changes the waist, the face and overall leanness.[1][6]

It works on the same pair of receptors as tirzepatide, the dual agonist already approved in the US as Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes (May 2022) and as Zepbound for weight management (November 2023).[6][5] Reviews discuss new co-agonists of this type as more potent weight-loss drugs than GLP-1 agonism alone.[7]

In a 13-week phase 2 trial in adults with obesity or overweight, mean weight loss ranged from 9.1% to 14.7% depending on dose, versus 1.7% with placebo.[1] Phase 3 trials started in 2025, and published studies are limited to medical trials in people with obesity, not cosmetic use.
infobox: Weekly subcutaneous injection; oral form in trials

paras: VK2735 is being studied for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight, and a separate phase 3 program covers people with type 2 diabetes.[8][9] No regulator has approved it.[5]

Within looksmaxxing and fitness discussion, GLP-1 and GIP-class drugs are talked about because large fat loss visibly changes the jawline, face and waist, and the same attention extends to pipeline drugs. VK2735 itself is not sold outside clinical trials and the registered studies enrol people with obesity rather than people seeking cosmetic leanness.[3][8]

VK2735 is a dual agonist of the GLP-1 receptor and the GIP receptor, with the same mechanism of action as tirzepatide.[5] In tirzepatide, Wikipedia describes stronger binding at the GIP receptor than at the GLP-1 receptor, with GLP-1 signalling favouring the cAMP pathway; weekly subcutaneous injection is the route for tirzepatide, and VK2735 is being tested in both injectable and oral forms.[6][5]

Viking Therapeutics is the developer of both the injectable and oral forms.[5] A phase 1 safety and tolerability study (NCT05203237) in 92 participants began in December 2021 and has been completed.[2] The phase 2 VENTURE study of the weekly injection started in August 2023, an oral phase 2 trial began in December 2024, and the phase 3 VANQUISH program began in June 2025.[3][4][8][9] A Reuters report on a successful weight-loss trial in 2024 is among the sources cited by Wikipedia's article.[5]

Oral phase 3 trials (SUNRISE 1 and 2) are registered with start dates in November 2026, and a further phase 1 study in adults with obesity but no other conditions began recruiting in November 2025.[10][11][12]
Phase 1: a phase 1 safety and tolerability study (NCT05203237) in 92 participants began in December 2021 and has been completed. [2]

Phase 2 (injection): the VENTURE trial was a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study of weekly subcutaneous VK2735 in adults with obesity or overweight and at least one weight-related condition, excluding diabetes. Conducted from August 2023 to February 2024, it reported mean weight reductions of 9.2 kg at the lowest dose and 14.6 kg at the highest, against 1.8 kg for placebo. [1][3] In the active groups, 93% of participants lost at least 5% of body weight, compared with 12% on placebo. [1]
Phase 2 (oral): a phase 2 trial of oral VK2735 (NCT06828055) enrolling 280 participants has been completed. [4]

Phase 3: registered phase 3 trials include a weight management study of about 4,500 participants, VANQUISH 2 in people with type 2 diabetes, and the oral SUNRISE 1 and 2 trials that were due to start in late 2026. [8][9][10][11] A further phase 1 study in obese adults without comorbidities is recruiting. [12]

For context, the approved comparator tirzepatide produced mean weight change of 15.0%, 19.5% and 20.9% at 72 weeks (5, 10 and 15 mg) versus 3.1% with placebo in the SURMOUNT-1 trial of adults without diabetes; the VENTURE figures come from a much shorter 13-week trial and are not a head-to-head comparison.[6][1]

The VENTURE trial report lists adverse events in the active groups; the trial was a short 13-week study, and its safety record beyond that period is the subject of the phase 3 program.[1][8] For the receptor class, Wikipedia's tirzepatide article lists nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, reduced appetite, constipation and abdominal pain as the most common effects, with discontinuation rising with dose in an earlier tirzepatide trial, and warns that the drug is contraindicated in people with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2.[6] These are class-level facts about tirzepatide, not trial results for VK2735.
Review authors discussing next-generation GLP-1 co-agonists note that cardiac effects of such drugs remain an area needing more research.[7]
VK2735 is an experimental drug available only to participants in registered clinical trials, and it has not been approved by the FDA or any other regulator.[2][3][8]

timeline.event: Phase 2 VENTURE trial begins in August. [3]
Phase 3 trials begin; an oral phase 2 trial starts in December 2024. [4][8][9]
